newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Coast Guard rescues German ship captain.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Coast Guard rescues German ship captain.

text.p: A German ship captain died early on Monday after suffering serious injuries while the ship pounded through six-to-nine foot (1.8-to 2.7 meters) seas off the coast of Massachusetts, the U.S. Coast Guard said.
The 55-year-old man, whose name was not released pending notification of relatives, was pronounced dead at a Cape Cod hospital, a Coast Guard spokesman said.

The man was the captain of the 500-foot (152-meter) commercial freighter Independent Pioneer, who was seriously injured while skippering the vessel some 280 miles (450 km) southeast of Cape Cod on Sunday. Crews aboard the ship tried to revive the man, who reportedly suffered an enormous blood loss from the fall.

"He was flown to a Cape Cod hospital early this morning where he was pronounced DOA (dead on arrival). He had had no pulse for four-and-a-half hours," said the spokesman Petty Officer Roger Wetherell.
The vessel was headed to Antwerp, Belgium, when the accident occurred. Wetherell said it would be up to the shipping agent to decide whether the German-flagged ship would continue on its course.
